87.title: Variation 87
sections: “Variation 87” is a living work by Nikolai Grigoriev. It turns a single life — the quiet traces one body leaves without being asked — slowly into an image, so that living can be seen and lived as a work of art. Its subject is not death but what death sharpens: the attention a life is worth once you know it ends. The work also belongs to a larger one: the lives it and its kind record gather into a collective form made to stand in a museum, a monument to attentive living — a shared dimension this work is made to join. A dated state is written “Variation 87, state of [date].” The work is one; its daily states are states of one work. Medium: software, lived time written daily by an unchanging rule, screen.

The rule and this certificate constitute the work. Any image, screen, or print is an execution of the rule — evidence of the work, not the work itself. Whoever holds this certificate holds the work; without this certificate there is no work.

Each day, the daily signal of one living body is turned into one painting. The seed of a day is drawn from the name of the artist, the date, and the day’s record together, by a fixed formula. Every day is weighed only against the days of this body’s own history that precede it — a hard day is hard by its own measure. The signals are entangled before they reach the canvas: every visible feature is driven by several at once, and no measurement can be read back out of the image. The same day always produces the same sequence of marks. Once a day has ended, its inputs never change — its painting never changes. The past stays frozen as it was written. The work never shows the present: a day is met only once it has closed and can no longer be performed for. This delay is not a limitation but the discipline of the work — it removes the audience, and what remains is presence.

The work accepts the daily signal of a living body from any instrument able to provide the schema of Appendix A. It is bound to no maker and no device. The artist is the sole subject of the signal in this work, by his own consent. Keeping the signal flowing is the duty of its subject; an interruption is not a breach — it is silence, and silence is part of the work. Appendix A — the exact schema of the daily signal — is printed only with the signed certificate and does not appear on any public surface of the work.

Mortality is not the work’s subject but its edge — the pressure that gives a life its attention. When no new day arrives, the work does not pretend. The last painting is held. From the second silent day its colour begins to leave; by the fourteenth the image stands without colour, and it goes on dissolving into the empty ground until, by the thirtieth silent day, nothing of it remains but the ground itself. The work is then empty, not finished. Any day that arrives restores it in full at once: the work returns as many times as the days do, and no silence is final. Silence is never declared from a stored record alone — only by the living programme itself — so a sleeping machine can never show a false death, and an instrument that has stopped is never painted as a body that has. Upon the certified death of the signal’s subject, the last state is permanent and the work is complete; the artist’s obligations do not survive the artist.

The subject of the signal may end his participation at any time. A declared withdrawal — a signed, dated statement, recorded in the provenance log — is written as silence from its date. The work registers absence, not its cause, and never names an undeclared silence a death. Withdrawal acts forward only: the days already written remain part of the work.

The work keeps every day it has lived. Each state is frozen as it was written on its own day; the future never repaints the past. Recorded gaps remain visible as gaps. The archive is the work’s memory and its full body — a life made imperishable as record, and one way the work lengthens a life in the only register art can reach.

This certificate transfers the work; re-registration of this document is the transfer. The bond to the artist’s body survives any sale: this work is not re-bound to another body. If the certificate is lost, one reissue may be made by the artist in person, recorded in the provenance log; after the artist, no reissue exists.

The artist maintains the performing programme and one working signal adapter for five years from the date of transfer. Thereafter the owner holds the complete rule, the code, the seed formula, and the schema of Appendix A — sufficient for any competent technician to perform any state of the work again.
Unique, 1/1. Daily states are states of this one work; they are not numbered and are not sold separately.
First recorded day 24 May 2022. The full provenance log, including earlier working titles, accompanies the signed certificate.

89.title: Variation 89

archipelago.title: Archipelago
sections: “Archipelago” is a living work by Nikolai Grigoriev. It is made from the only hours of a day in which a person cannot pose. The rest of the time a life is presented; a pose is held with muscle, attention and will, and in sleep there is nothing left to hold it with. The instrument does not record a picture of the man — it records what is left of him when the pose cannot be held. Its subject is not sleep and not health: it is the part of a life that no one, including the one living it, is performing. A dated state is written “Archipelago, state of [date],” naming the night that made it. The work is one; its nightly states are states of one work. Medium: software, a sleeping body written nightly by an unchanging rule, screen.

The rule and this certificate constitute the work. Any image, screen, or print is an execution of the rule — evidence of the work, not the work itself. Whoever holds this certificate holds the work; without this certificate there is no work.

Each night of one sleeping body is turned into one painting. Every five minutes of sleep is one charge: its weight is the depth of those minutes, its radius the body’s recovery in them. The painting is the level set of their sum — while the body keeps returning, neighbouring minutes merge into one mass; when it stops, the mass falls apart into islands. Nothing decides whether a night is one body or an archipelago except the night. The hours awake are not drawn: they only part. Falling asleep occupies its true place at the head and stays empty. The light along the edge is the pulse of those minutes, read against that night’s own floor, because the heart is the one thing the body never switches off. The seed of a night is drawn from that night alone; the date plays no part in it. The same night always makes the same painting, and a night already painted is never repainted. The instrument’s own verdict on the night — its score — is not used anywhere in the work.

The work accepts the nightly signal of a sleeping body from any instrument able to provide the schema of Appendix A: the sequence of sleep stages, the movement, the recovery and the heart, at the resolution the schema states. It is bound to no maker and no device. The artist is the sole subject of the signal in this work, by his own consent. A day the instrument recorded without sleep is not a night this work can paint and does not enter its calendar; that is not a gap in the record but the absence of its material.

When no night arrives, the work does not pretend. The last painting is held. From the second silent day the edge goes out first — the pulse is the first thing to stop being visible, because it is the only thing that was never a state the body entered and left. The mass follows it, losing density until nothing is left but the ground. The ground of this work is the dark itself, present from its first night as material and not as metaphor; so its empty canvas is that dark, and the work ends as a night with nobody in it. The work is then empty, not finished. Any night that arrives restores it in full at once, and no silence is final. Silence is never declared from a stored record alone — only by the living programme — so an instrument that has stopped is never painted as a body that has. This work counts its own silence, from its own last night, and never from the daily record of the same body.

The subject of the signal may end his participation at any time. A declared withdrawal — a signed, dated statement, recorded in the provenance log — is written as silence from its date. The work registers absence, not its cause, and never names an undeclared silence a death. Withdrawal acts forward only: the nights already written remain part of the work.

The work keeps every night it has lived, written once and never rewritten; the future never repaints the past. Recorded gaps remain visible as gaps. The archive is the work’s memory and its full body.

This certificate transfers the work; re-registration of this document is the transfer. The bond to the artist’s body survives any sale: this work is not re-bound to another body. If the certificate is lost, one reissue may be made by the artist in person, recorded in the provenance log; after the artist, no reissue exists.

The artist maintains the performing programme and one working signal adapter for five years from the date of transfer of this certificate. Thereafter the owner holds the complete rule, the code, the seed formula, and the schema of Appendix A — sufficient for any competent technician to perform any state of the work again.
Unique, 1/1. Nightly states are states of this one work; they are not numbered and are not sold separately.
